messages:
support_jan: Heads up — AcmeAnalytics reported a large spike of 502/504s hitting Redwood hosted inference in us-west1 starting ~09:42 UTC. They see consistent gateway timeouts and internal 5xx on text generation routes. Customer is P0. Can SRE triage? Logs attached to the ticket: gateway 504, "no ready pods" errors, queue depth > 200.
oncall_dave: Acknowledged. I'll start with HPA/KEDA checks. Can you paste an example request id or exact call time? I'll check autoscale history and kube events.
support_jan: Request ids: req-xx-7a3 and req-xx-7a4 around 09:42:12 and 09:42:45. Customer says intermittent success but large tail latency leading to client timeouts (30s). They mention surge traffic from a nightly job.
marta_sre: I see the gateway logs for req-xx-7a3: "upstream: no route to host / no healthy upstream" then 504. Kube events show a burst of scaling events 09:41:55 -> 09:43:30 but many pods stayed NotReady for 30-60s.
alex_dev: NotReady likely due to model init. Do we have model-init logs? Which model variant were they hitting?
support_jan: They hit "redwood/rlhf-7b:quant" (customer pinned). Looks like initial pod images pulled fine, but container liveness/readiness interplay suspicious.
raj_infra: Pull times look normal. I'll describe one of the failing pods.
raj_infra: ```
$ kubectl describe pod acme-gen-7b-5f9
Events:
  Warning  Unhealthy  20s   kubelet, ip-10-0-2-14  Readiness probe failed: HTTPGet /healthz 503
  Normal   Started    15s   kubelet, ip-10-0-2-14  Started container
  Warning  BackOff    10s   kubelet, ip-10-0-2-14  Back-off restarting failed container
Logs:
  [2026-03-15T09:41:58Z] Loading model weights... (this can take ~40s)
  [2026-03-15T09:42:40Z] Model runtime initialized, KV cache warm incomplete, serving disabled until cache ready
  [2026-03-15T09:42:55Z] Readiness probe failing: warmup-check failed
```
marta_sre: That matches. Model init ~40s then additional warmup/kvcache steps another 10-20s. Meanwhile KEDA scaled from 0->8 quickly but HPA stabilization and Kube scheduler+node provisioning added 20-30s. Gateway has no available pods for some requests -> 504.
oncall_dave: So root cause looks like mismatch of provisioning ramp and per-pod warmup window. Also check KEDA config: pollingInterval, cooldownPeriod, and trigger type (queue length?). If polling interval is long we can under/overshoot.
ops-bot: KEDA ScaledObject: pollInterval=30s, cooldownPeriod=60s, minReplicaCount=0, maxReplicaCount=20, triggers: rabbitmq-queue-length targetAverageValue=50
alex_dev: pollInterval 30s is high for a bursty queue. If the queue jumps, KEDA might take up to 30s to notice then spawn pods which take ~60s to be ready => large tail.
marta_sre: Also HPA metrics server has a stabilization window of 60s. We saw a scale event at 09:41:55 and readiness didn't converge until ~09:43:20. Meanwhile gateway timed out on requests at 09:42:12.
nate_ml: For this model variant, cold start includes JIT/quant kernel init and KV cache population which is expensive. There is a warmup endpoint we can call to pre-initialize after container started. We should exercise that during startup so readiness is only declared after warmup.
oncall_dave: Quick mitigations: 1) increase minReplicaCount to 2 for the pool (avoid 0->many coldstart), 2) reduce KEDA pollInterval to 5s and cooldownPeriod to 20s, 3) add a prewarm job that calls /internal/warmup on new pods from a sidecar or init container, 4) temporarily increase gateway timeout to 45s for this customer. Can infra do 1 & 2 now? If successful, will reduce error rate quickly.
raj_infra: I'll patch scaledobject for that model pool in us-west1 to minReplicaCount=2 and pollInterval=5s now. Applying as emergency change.
deploy-bot: Patch applied: scaledobject.acme-pool (us-west1) set minReplicaCount=2, pollInterval=5s, cooldownPeriod=20s — triggered rollout ID dpl-20260315-01
oncall_dave: Monitoring the metrics — queue depth dropping, pod count stable at 3 (2 warm + 1 extra). Gateway 5xxs rate decreasing.
emily_customer_success: I've updated AcmeAnalytics with a brief status note: "We've applied mitigations (min replicas + faster scaler polling) and are seeing error rates drop. We will follow up with a postmortem and permanent fix timeline." They replied :thumbsup: and asked for concrete RCA.
alex_dev: Permanent fixes to include: change readiness probe to check model runtime + KV warm flag (not just port), add init warmup curl in startup, and document recommended minReplicaCount for models with >20s init time. Also evaluate keeping small baseline pool for high-traffic customers.
nate_ml: I'll open a PR to runtime that exposes /internal/warmup + graceful readiness gating. I'll add default warmup-curl in Helm chart for heavy models.
marta_sre: Root cause summary for postmortem: KEDA/HPA/provisioning ramp mismatch combined with long model cold-start/warmup. KEDA pollInterval too coarse and minReplicaCount=0 allowed complete coldstart. Result: request backlog, gateway timeouts (504) and 5xxs. Mitigations applied and customer updated.
support_jan: Customer confirmed errors dropped to near zero after the change. Closing P0 but requesting a postmortem. Assigning to eng-runtime + eng-releases for follow-up.
oncall_dave: I'll draft incident timeline and add to /incidents and link to this thread. Will include repro steps and the kube commands we used.
support_jan: Repro steps saved: 1) simulate queue spike -> publish 500 msgs to rabbit queue, 2) watch KEDA poll log, 3) kubectl get pods -w in pool ns, 4) tail gateway logs for 504s. Saved as note in ticket.
marta_sre: I'll schedule a short runbook update: recommend pollInterval <=5s for queue-triggered scaling for high-sensitivity pools, minReplicaCount >=1 for models with init>15s, and document warmup endpoint usage.
support_jan: Great team, thanks. I'll send a customer-facing RCA after postmortem. Closing thread in 24h unless further spikes.
